Chinese Pork and Cabbage Dumplings (Jiaozi)

Served at: Perchta Day (Perchtenlauf) · Lunar New Year (Chunjie)

Approximately 40-50 dumplings, serving 4-6Prep 60 minutesCook 10-15 minutes per batch

These savory dumplings, known as Jiaozi, are a cornerstone of Lunar New Year celebrations (Chunjie), symbolizing wealth and prosperity due to their shape resembling ancient gold ingots. Families gather to make and enjoy them, fostering togetherness and good fortune for the coming year. While not traditionally associated with Perchta Day (Perchtenlauf), their hearty and comforting nature makes them a perfect, warming meal for any cold winter festival.

Ingredients

  • For the Dough:
  • 2 cups (240g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) warm water (about 100-110°F / 38-43°C)
  • Pinch of salt
  • For the Filling:
  • 1 pound (450g) ground pork (medium fat content is best)
  • 2 cups (about 1/2 small head) finely chopped napa cabbage
  • 2-3 green onions, thinly sliced
  • 1 inch (2.5cm) fresh ginger, grated
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tablespoons light soy sauce
  • 1 tablespoon sesame oil
  • 1/2 teaspoon white pepper
  • For the Dipping Sauce:
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) light soy sauce
  • 2 tablespoons (30ml) rice vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon (5ml) sesame oil
  • Chili oil, to taste (optional)

Method

  1. Prepare the Dough: In a large bowl, combine flour and salt. Gradually add warm water, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover with plastic wrap and let rest for at least 30 minutes at room temperature.
  2. Prepare the Cabbage: Place the finely chopped napa cabbage in a bowl. Sprinkle with 1/2 teaspoon of salt and let sit for 10 minutes. Squeeze out as much excess water as possible from the cabbage using your hands or a clean kitchen towel. This prevents the filling from becoming watery.
  3. Make the Filling: In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, squeezed cabbage, green onions, grated ginger, minced garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, and white pepper. Mix thoroughly with your hands or a spoon until all ingredients are well combined and slightly sticky.
  4. Form the Wrappers: Divide the rested dough into two equal portions. Roll one portion into a long log (about 1 inch / 2.5 cm diameter). Cut the log into 20-25 equal pieces. Flatten each piece into a small disc. On a lightly floured surface, roll each disc into a thin, round wrapper (about 3-4 inches / 7-10 cm in diameter), keeping the edges slightly thinner than the center. Repeat with the second dough portion.
  5. Fill and Fold the Dumplings: Hold a wrapper in the palm of your hand. Place about 1 tablespoon of filling in the center. Moisten half of the wrapper edge with a little water. Fold the wrapper in half to create a crescent shape. Pinch the center closed, then make small pleats along one side of the wrapper, pressing them firmly against the other side to seal completely. Ensure no air is trapped inside. Place finished dumplings on a lightly floured baking sheet, making sure they don't touch.
  6. Cook the Dumplings (Boiling Method): Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Carefully add 10-15 dumplings, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Stir gently to prevent sticking. Once the water returns to a boil, add about 1/2 cup (120ml) cold water. Repeat this process two more times. The dumplings are cooked when they float to the surface and appear plump (about 8-10 minutes total). Remove with a slotted spoon.
  7. Cook the Dumplings (Pan-Frying/Potsticker Method): Heat 1-2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Place dumplings in a single layer, flat side down, and cook for 2-3 minutes until the bottoms are golden brown. Add about 1/2 cup (120ml) of water to the skillet, immediately cover with a lid, and steam for 5-7 minutes, or until the water has evaporated and the dumplings are cooked through. Remove the lid and cook for another minute to crisp the bottoms.
  8. Prepare the Dipping Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame oil. Add chili oil to taste, if desired.
  9. Serve: Serve the hot dumplings immediately with the dipping sauce.

Tips

  • Freezing Dumplings: Uncooked dumplings can be frozen. Place them on a floured baking sheet and freeze until solid, then transfer to an airtight freezer bag. Cook from frozen, adding a few extra minutes to the cooking time.
  • Filling Variations: Experiment with different fillings! You can substitute ground chicken or shrimp, or add finely chopped mushrooms, carrots, or bok choy for more flavor and texture.
  • Perfect Pleats: Don't worry if your first few dumplings aren't perfect. Practice makes perfect! The key is to ensure a tight seal to keep the delicious filling inside.
